Mode == 1: HasOffsetMapping checks UID5 presence; GetOffsetMapping retrieves UID6, with a virtual regeneration attempt if absent. Mode != 1: those paths check/retrieve UID3 directly.

UID5 UUID 8d56827c-847e-11d5-935a-50f857c10000 is the speed graph; UID6 UUID 8d56827d-847e-11d5-935a-50f857c10000 is its prepared output-to-source offset graph. UID3 UUID 8d56827a-847e-11d5-935a-50f857c10000 serves directly as the alternate graph offset mapping. Its formal UI label was not independently proved by these four bodies.

GetOffsetMappingAdjustment returns 0 for mode 1 and the stored offset_adjust for the other graph mode. Prepared UID6 fallback does not separately add constant-SPED phase. Do not apply inactive UI graph or phase twice.
The existence of a populated UID6 is not by itself a freshness certificate or proof that the live effect callback uses that exact fallback.

callbackFindings.finding: Base AEffect::GetOffsetMinMax calls virtual slot 0x230, proven vtable symbol DoesTimeWarp(int), using the requested input-track argument. If false, outputs inclusive start and start+length-1.

When DoesTimeWarp is true, base AEffect computes a min/max envelope by calling virtual MapOffsetDown for every integer output position t in [start,start+length), for both videoField values 0 and 1. Floating results are truncated toward zero; min/max outputs are inclusive. It computes the first field once to initialize. This is an envelope, not a list of all individual samples.
Base AEffect::MapOffsetDown returns t for field 0 and t+0.5 when the field argument equals 1.

AVX2Effect::MapOffsetDown attempts an external remapping interface callback only when object+0x3b8 is non-null AND GetAVX2Instance(EffectInterface*) returns non-null. It uses the instance effect context at +0x30 and interface slot +0x20. A negative callback status falls back to t or t+0.5. Success takes one of the two returned field offsets. Field-conversion helper implementation was not inspected.

AVX2Effect::GetOffsetMinMax uses the same two pointer gates. It constructs callback endpoints [start,start+length-1] for positive length; for non-positive length the callback end is start. The callback is external; its sample support, graph freshness and reconstruction rules are not established by these call sites.

After successful AVX2 range remapping, if neither IsVDMEffect() nor IsAcplEffect() is true, returned min/max are widened to include the original requested start and inclusive end. If the clamp argument is set, low is clamped to >=0 and high to <=EffectInterface length-1.

Absent remapping interface or absent AVX2 instance: AVX2 range fallback outputs start and start+length-1. Callback failure skips success widening/clamping and leaves the initialized request envelope. This method does not inspect serialized SPED effect_id, source_param_list or new_source_calculation directly.

savedMapFallbackFormula.provenance: Re-expression of already-recorded AMotionCtl::MapRangeDown and AParamClip::GetDoubleMinMax anchors, not an additional newly inspected method.
savedMapFallbackFormula.domain: Nonempty requested [a,a+n), finite min/max, positive finite representable child length L, no adaptive-deinterlace expansion. Unsupported/invalid numeric cases are not certified.
savedMapFallbackFormula.extrema: The no-effect prepared-map fallback evaluates map(a) AND map(a+n), plus stored key values inside that interval. The upper evaluation is inclusive in this fallback, even though a+n is the exclusive output endpoint.
savedMapFallbackFormula.formula: v = min(mapMinimum, L-1); signedEpsilon = (v < 0 ? -1e-6 : +1e-6); lower = truncTowardZero(max(0, v + signedEpsilon)); upperCandidate = min(L, max(mapMaximum,0)+1); count = ceil(upperCandidate-lower-1e-6); returned half-open source range = [lower, lower+count).
savedMapFallbackFormula.adaptiveDeinterlace: Earlier native anchors optionally subtract one from minimum and add one to maximum before the formula, subject to supported rate and adaptive-deinterlace gates.
savedMapFallbackFormula.endpointCaveat: The main effect callback can return an inclusive discrete last source sample, whereas the no-effect numeric-curve fallback includes the value at output a+n before adding one. These routes cannot be assumed equivalent at a nested cut boundary.

actualUseAndActionableLimits: Native range methods return one min/max envelope. They do not encode holes between sampled source positions. Neither a fast linear mapping nor a discontinuity may be assumed to consume every intervening nested clip just because it lies inside that envelope.

A continuous linear curve alone does not settle the discrete support of an active effect: field processing, interpolation and plugin callback decisions can affect support. This bounded audit therefore does not certify exact nested-edit membership for general saved maps, including speed 2x or jumps.

Safe current implementation boundary remains: independently proved terminal physical originals/renders may be kept, while uncertain nested time branches remain explicit gaps. Do not silently widen to the whole source sequence or use inactive graphs.

If implementing prepared-map range envelopes as a distinct policy, name them as native range envelopes and obtain the required actual-use decision/validation; do not claim an exact per-frame or per-camera used set from min/max alone.

No callback applicability test based only on serialized effect_id, source_param_list or new_source_calculation was established. The inspected AVX2 call sites gate on runtime pointers/instances. Proving how serialized SPED creates those instances needs additional scope and was intentionally not attempted.
